queries: WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_invoiced_orders_above_avg, AVG(g.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.cnt > a.avg_cnt

WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), avg_all AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS a FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_invoiced_orders, AVG(g.cnt - avg_all.a) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM g CROSS JOIN avg_all WHERE g.cnt > avg_all.a

WITH per_gender AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM per_gender) SELECT AVG(p.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_invoiced_orders_above_avg, AVG(p.cnt - ov.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM per_gender p CROSS JOIN overall ov WHERE p.cnt > ov.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: A NULL gender forms its own group (GROUP BY keeps NULLs together); empty-string genders, if any, remain a separate group from NULL.
Only orders with at least one invoice are counted (inner join from Invoices), and each order is counted once per gender via COUNT(DISTINCT order_id).
If no gender is above the average (e.g., all counts equal or only one group), the query returns one row with NULL averages.

assumptions.assumption: Only orders with at least one invoice are counted (inner join from Invoices), and a NULL gender forms its own group via GROUP BY. Empty-string gender is treated as a distinct value from NULL.
If no gender is above the average (e.g., all counts equal), the query returns one row with NULL values.

responses.sql: WITH per_gender AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM per_gender) SELECT AVG(p.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_invoiced_orders_above_avg, AVG(p.cnt - ov.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM per_gender p CROSS JOIN overall ov WHERE p.cnt > ov.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: A NULL gender forms its own group (GROUP BY keeps NULLs together). Empty-string genders are kept as a separate group from NULL, as stored.
The overall average is the plain unweighted average of per-gender counts, including the missing-gender group, over genders that have at least one invoiced order.
If no gender exceeds the average (e.g. all counts equal), the query returns one row with NULL values rather than zero rows.
